claim: LeNet paper identifies local receptive fields, shared weights and subsampling as key architectural ideas
Original LeNet-5 stage shapes are 32x32, C1 6@28x28, S2 6@14x14, C3 16@10x10, S4 16@5x5, C5 120, F6 84, output 10
S2/S4 are learned subsampling layers with trainable coefficient, bias and nonlinearity
Original C3 has partial connections and 1516 trainable parameters
LeNet-5 final output uses Euclidean RBF penalties and scaled tanh hidden activations
Paper describes 345308 connections and about 60000 independent parameters
Toy 5x5 by 3x3 cross correlation has top-left outputs -1 and 0
locator: Section II-A mechanism; independent illustrative numbers
notes: Assertions in mini_cnn.py, not the original paper's values.

claim: Standard dense convolution with bias uses Cout*(Cin*Kh*Kw+1) trainable parameters
notes: Explicitly excludes grouped and partial connections.

claim: AlexNet NeurIPS 2012 official abstract reports top-1 39.7% and top-5 18.9% error on LSVRC-2010 test
notes: Not a direct comparable benchmark with ResNet 2015.

claim: VGG explores depth using small convolutional filters
ResNet reports 3.57 percent top-5 error for an ensemble on the ILSVRC 2015 test

notes: Only one-channel valid stride-one formula shown; numerical check in minimal code.

claim: Applying the 3x3 teaching kernel with rows [1,0,-1] to the fixed 5x5 matrix at valid stride 1 yields the complete output map [[-1,0,1],[-1,2,0],[1,0,-1]]; each output is nine input-kernel products summed using shared weights.
locator: Independent arithmetic in article Section 03, informed by the 1998 paper's Section II on local receptive fields and shared weights
